project.name: ByteRush
project.subtitle: Autonomous ML Research Agent for Recommender Systems
project.tagline: From an FM baseline to a verified, submission-ready ranking model.

story.problem: Recommendation research is usually a slow manual loop of proposing, coding, training, evaluating, and deciding what to try next.
story.solution: ByteRush turns that loop into an autonomous, evidence-guided search while keeping model selection validation-only.
story.winner_summary: The winning Wide & Deep model combines a memorization path for frequent interactions with a nonlinear path for higher-order feature combinations.
takeaways: Diverse model roots prevented the search from being trapped in the original FM family.
Controlled tuning promoted Wide & Deep before creative research continued around the new incumbent.
Multi-seed verification confirmed stability before the model and submission were frozen.

winner.label: Wide & Deep
winner.principal_change: A wide linear path captures memorized interactions while a deep path learns nonlinear feature combinations.

nodes.label: Replace the FM model with a lightweight Deep & Cross N…
nodes.hypothesis: Replace the FM model with a lightweight Deep & Cross Network (DCN) that captures explicit feature crosses with a cross network and nonlinear transformations with a deep network, while preserving the input schema, pointwise BCE loss, and validation-only evaluation. The data flow remains the same: categorical feature IDs input to embedding layers, then fed into the DCN model producing logits for BCE loss. The training loop and checkpointing are unchanged except for a 5-epoch cap per bootstrap constraints. The DCN model is registered as an ablation component and guarded accordingly. This controlled architectural change tests the hypothesis that DCN improves validation ranking metrics over FM under the same protocol.

nodes.label: A hybrid pointwise and pairwise ranking objective can …
nodes.hypothesis: A hybrid pointwise and pairwise ranking objective can better align training with the GAUC/nDCG metrics by encouraging correct ordering within the same user. We will implement a new ablation component "ranking_objective_component" that replaces the pure BCE loss with a combined BCE + BPR pairwise loss. The BPR loss will be computed over positive-negative pairs sampled within each batch restricted to the same user, using the first feature column as user_id. This preserves the existing FM model architecture and feature inputs but changes the loss path. The training loop will remain unchanged except for the loss computation in step(). All other invariants including data loading, evaluation, checkpointing, and validation primary metric remain protected.

nodes.label: Implementation plan: We hypothesize that adding causal…
nodes.hypothesis:
Implementation plan:
We hypothesize that adding causal recent user history features (e.g., recent author, tag, duration, and recency profiles) and a lightweight DIN-style interest encoder consuming their embeddings will improve validation ranking metrics (GAUC and nDCG@5). We will extend the build_features function to attach these causal history factors using research_data.attach_causal_history, producing new integer ID fields for recent authors and tags, and recency buckets. The CandidateModel will be replaced by a WideDeepModel that embeds these new history features alongside the original 5 fields, concatenates all embeddings, and passes them through a small MLP to produce logits. This new model path will be guarded by a new ablation component 'causal_history_interest_component'. We preserve all existing training, evaluation, checkpointing, and validation protocols, ensuring no leakage by building history only from strictly earlier events and freezing feature state after train. This approach respects the input contract and is expected to improve GAUC primarily by modeling recent user interests.

nodes.label: A controlled hybrid ranking objective combining pointw…
nodes.hypothesis: A controlled hybrid ranking objective combining pointwise BCE and pairwise BPR loss is implemented to better align training with the GAUC/nDCG metrics. The model remains the existing FM embedding architecture, but the loss computation is extended to include a pairwise BPR term computed over same-user positive-negative pairs extracted from the batch. User IDs are read from the first feature column to build masks for valid pairs. The pairwise loss is weighted and added to the BCE loss, guarded by an ablation component. All other training, evaluation, and checkpointing protocols remain unchanged and protected. This approach tests whether adding a pairwise ranking signal improves validation primary metrics without changing model capacity or features.

This transfer tests if adding DCN interactions improves validation GAUC and nDCG@5 over the wide_deep baseline without disrupting existing infrastructure.
